item.title: Enterprise Self-Hosted Supabase
item.description:
Pigsty can deploy Supabase on your physical, virtual, or cloud servers with a single command. Self-hosting provides more extensions, performance options, control, and potential cost savings.

As of August 2026, the official Supabase self-hosting guide recommends Docker and classifies other implementations as community projects. Pigsty is an independent community integration and is not currently listed on that page.

This tutorial requires basic Linux knowledge. Otherwise, consider using Supabase cloud or plain Docker Compose self-hosting.

item.title: Odoo: Self-Hosted Open Source ERP
item.description:
Odoo is open-source ERP software with CRM, sales, inventory, and other business applications. The template stays on Odoo Community 19.0 for addon compatibility and uses PostgreSQL 18.

Odoo 19 requires PostgreSQL 13 or later and Python 3.10 or later; the official Docker image provides Python.

Quick Start

On a fresh Linux x86_64 / ARM64 server running a compatible operating system:

curl -fsSL https://repo.pigsty.io/get | bash; cd ~/pigsty
./bootstrap # Install Ansible
./configure -c app/odoo # Generate the Odoo configuration
vi pigsty.yml # Change default passwords
./deploy.yml # Install Pigsty and PostgreSQL
./docker.yml # Install Docker Compose
./app.yml # Initialize the Odoo database and start the web container

Port 8069 is published on all host interfaces by default. Open http://<ip>:8069. The initial application login is admin / admin; change the password at first login.

item.title: Dify: AI Workflow Platform
item.description:
Dify is an open-source platform for developing generative AI and LLM applications. It supports agent creation, AI workflows, RAG retrieval, and model management. These features help users build and operate generative AI applications.

Pigsty supports self-hosted Dify with single-command deployment. Critical state resides in externally managed PostgreSQL. You can use pgvector in the same PostgreSQL instance as the vector database to simplify deployment.

  • Quick Start
  • Why Self-Host
  • Installation
  • Configuration
  • Checklist
  • Domain and SSL
  • Upgrading
  • File Backup

The template uses Dify v1.17.1 with plugin daemon v0.6.10-local and sandbox v0.2.15. Validation on 2026-10-08 covered login, an existing Code workflow, and service connections on Linux amd64 with PostgreSQL 18.6. Dify v1.16 and later handle PostgreSQL 18’s built-in uuidv7() without a local migration patch.

item.title: InsForge: AI Backend-as-a-Service
item.description:
InsForge is an open-source Backend-as-a-Service platform for AI coding agents, built around PostgreSQL. It provides authentication, database APIs, file storage, a model gateway, edge functions, site deployment, and payment integrations. These features reduce common backend implementation work.

Pigsty provides the app/insforge template. It runs stateless InsForge OSS services in Docker Compose and stores critical state in Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL. This provides high availability, backup and recovery, monitoring, ingress domains, and infrastructure services. The database does not depend on an ephemeral container volume.

item.title: Hindsight: AI Long-Term Memory
item.description:
Hindsight is a PostgreSQL-native long-term memory service for AI agents.

Pigsty provides the app/hindsight configuration template (conf/app/hindsight.yml). By default, it uses Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL instead of Hindsight’s built-in development database.

Quick Start 

curl -fsSL https://repo.pigsty.io/get | bash; cd ~/pigsty
./bootstrap
./configure -c app/hindsight
vi pigsty.yml # edit domain, database password, and LLM settings
./deploy.yml
./docker.yml
./app.yml

Default access URLs:

  • UI: http://hs.pigsty or http://<IP>:9999
  • API: http://hs-api.pigsty or http://<IP>:8888

item.title: FerretDB: MongoDB Protocol
item.description:
FerretDB provides a MongoDB-compatible protocol over PostgreSQL and the DocumentDB extension. Pigsty’s app/ferretdb runs the stateless protocol proxy. PostgreSQL, the postgres database, DocumentDB extensions, and a backend PostgreSQL login role must already exist. The fork/mongo configuration template prepares these dependencies together.

curl -fsSL https://repo.pigsty.io/get | bash; cd ~/pigsty
./bootstrap
./configure -c fork/mongo
./deploy.yml
./docker.yml -l pg-meta
./app.yml -l pg-meta

item.title: Gitea: Self-Hosted Git Service
item.description:
Gitea is a lightweight open-source Git hosting platform.

Pigsty’s app/gitea template uses external PostgreSQL mode by default. Configure the database through GITEA_DB_* values in .env.

cd ~/pigsty/app/gitea

make up

Default endpoints:

item.title: NocoDB: Open-Source Airtable
item.description:
NocoDB is an open-source Airtable alternative that turns any database into a smart spreadsheet.

Use its visual interface to create database applications without code. NocoDB supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and other databases. You can use it for internal tools and data management systems.

Quick Start

Pigsty provides a Docker Compose configuration file for NocoDB in the software template directory:

cd ~/pigsty/app/nocodb

Review and modify the .env configuration file (adjust database connections as needed).

item.title: Wiki.js: OSS Wiki Software
item.description:
Public Demo: http://wiki.pigsty.cc

The current Compose uses the untagged requarks/wiki image. Stable 2.x releases are maintained in requarks/wiki-v2; the original requarks/wiki repository contains 3.x Beta releases. The image resolved to 2.5.316 during validation on 2026-10-08. Record and verify the actual image version before production upgrades.

TL; DR 

cd ~/pigsty/app/wiki && docker compose up -d

Postgres Preparation 

# postgres://dbuser_wiki:DBUser.Wiki@10.10.10.10:5432/wiki
- { name: wiki, owner: dbuser_wiki, revokeconn: true , comment: wiki the api gateway database }
- { name: dbuser_wiki, password: DBUser.Wiki , pgbouncer: true , roles: [ dbrole_admin ] }
bin/pgsql-user pg-meta dbuser_wiki
bin/pgsql-db pg-meta wiki

Configuration 

services:
 wiki:
 container_name: wiki
 image: requarks/wiki
 environment:
 DB_TYPE: postgres
 DB_HOST: 10.10.10.10
 DB_PORT: 5432
 DB_USER: dbuser_wiki
 DB_PASS: DBUser.Wiki
 DB_NAME: wiki
 restart: unless-stopped
 ports:
 - "9002:3000"

Access

  • Default Port for wiki: 9002
infra_portal:
 wiki: { domain: wiki.pigsty.io, endpoint: "127.0.0.1:9002" }
./infra.yml -t nginx_config,nginx_reload -l infra

item.title: Maybe: Self-Hosted Personal Finance
item.description:
Maybe is an open-source personal finance application. It manages accounts, transactions, budgets, investments, and household financial views. This Rails application stores production business data in PostgreSQL and uses Redis for background job queues.

Pigsty’s app/maybe template connects stateless Maybe Web / Worker containers to Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL. Local Redis provides the Sidekiq queue. Financial data resides in a PostgreSQL cluster with backup, monitoring, and recovery support, rather than an ephemeral Docker volume.

item.title: Immich: Self-Hosted Photo and Video Library
item.description:
Immich is a high-performance, self-hosted photo and video management application. It is a popular open-source alternative to Google Photos, licensed under AGPL-3.0. Features include web and mobile uploads, album sharing, timelines, maps, EXIF and RAW support, and LivePhoto. It also provides semantic search, facial recognition, and automatic backups.

Pigsty’s app/immich template runs the Immich application layer with Docker Compose and stores metadata in Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL. The template follows Immich v3 and uses VectorChord by default for similar-image search, smart search, and face-search vectors. On 2026-10-08, both Server and ML images resolved to 3.3.0. Validation used a new media library on Linux amd64 with PostgreSQL 18.6 and covered uploads, thumbnails, and real machine-learning inference.

item.title: Metabase: BI Analytics Tool
item.description:
Metabase is an open-source business intelligence tool. Teams can quickly explore and visualize data through its interface without SQL knowledge.

Metabase provides many chart types and connects to different databases. These features support enterprise data analysis.

The template defaults to metabase/metabase:v0.64.1.x. Use the single METABASE_IMAGE setting to override the full image reference. On 2026-10-08, the tag resolved to 0.64.1.1; validation on PostgreSQL 18.6 covered upgrading a restored metadata database, login, and querying an existing saved question.

item.title: JumpServer: Open-Source Bastion Host
item.description:
JumpServer is an open-source PAM and bastion-host system. It manages centralized access to SSH, RDP, database, and web assets. Pigsty’s app/jumpserver template runs Community Edition application containers with Docker Compose. Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL provides persistent database storage.

The template uses JumpServer v5.0.0-ce. It retains Community Edition core, celery, koko, kael, chen, and web services, plus local Redis. It removes the upstream installer’s built-in PostgreSQL service. Pigsty manages PostgreSQL, backups, monitoring, Nginx ingress, and the database lifecycle.

item.title: ByteBase: Schema Migration
item.description:
Bytebase is a database schema change and version management tool.

Pigsty provides a Compose template in app/bytebase. It listens on 8887 by default and uses BB_PGURL to connect to external PostgreSQL.

Quick Start 

cd ~/pigsty/app/bytebase
vi .env # check BB_PORT / BB_DOMAIN / BB_PGURL
make up

Access:

  • http://ddl.pigsty
  • http://<IP>:8887

After the first start, use the Bytebase setup wizard to initialize the admin account.

item.title: pgAdmin: PostgreSQL GUI
item.description:
pgAdmin is an open-source PostgreSQL administration and development GUI. Pigsty v4.5.0 provides the app/pgadmin Docker Compose template. It can generate a server list and password file from the current inventory.

Change the defaults first

The template login is admin@pigsty.cc with password pigsty. It is suitable only for a local demo. Before deployment on a shared network or the Internet, change the credentials, restrict port access, and configure HTTPS.

item.title: Electric: PostgreSQL Sync Engine
item.description:
Electric is a PostgreSQL sync engine. It delivers database changes efficiently to frontend and edge applications.

Pigsty provides the app/electric template (conf/app/electric.yml). It configures the database, containers, and ingress in one workflow.

Quick Start 

curl -fsSL https://repo.pigsty.io/get | bash; cd ~/pigsty
./bootstrap
./configure -c app/electric
vi pigsty.yml # update domain, passwords, secrets
./deploy.yml
./docker.yml
./app.yml

  • http://<IP>:8002
  • http://elec.pigsty (default domain in the template)

Metrics port defaults to 8003 (ELECTRIC_PROMETHEUS_PORT).

item.title: Jupyter: Notebooks and Data Analysis
item.description:
JupyterLab is an interactive notebook, terminal, and data-analysis environment. Pigsty v4.5.0 has two distinct deployment paths:

  • The VIBE module, managed by Ansible and systemd, for the complete v4.5.0 development sandbox.
  • The lightweight standalone app/jupyter Docker Compose template documented here.

app/jupyter is not a default apps inventory entry. Prepare its data directory separately. app.yml -e app=jupyter does not handle directory ownership.

Quick Start 

cd ~/pigsty/app/jupyter
vi .env # change JUPYTER_TOKEN and optionally pin JUPYTER_IMAGE
chmod 600 .env
make dir # create /data/jupyter, owned by 1000:100
make up # docker compose up -d

Generate a strong token with openssl rand -hex 32. The default port is 8888; open http://<host_ip>:8888.

item.title: Supabase
item.description:
Supabase — Build in a weekend, Scale to millions

Supabase is an open-source Firebase alternative built on PostgreSQL. It provides authentication, ready-to-use APIs, edge functions, real-time subscriptions, object storage, and vector embeddings. The low-code backend platform can replace much of the backend development work. Database design and frontend knowledge can be sufficient to build a product.

Supabase’s motto is: “Build in a weekend, Scale to millions”. Its cloud service can be cost-effective for small deployments, such as 4c8g. For millions of users, consider self-hosting to meet functionality, performance, and cost requirements.
